audit.why: Olaf takes level 1 on Undertow plus Reckless Swing true damage against zero resistances, Cassiopeia takes level 3 once the Q-into-Twin-Fang loop is online, and everything from 4 onward is a genuine skill row because Ragnarok answers her ultimate. That matches 49.12% over 114 games - the most honest chart in my slice - and both layers agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Undertow is the named matchup-defining cooldown in four fields with no number, Ragnarok is called the all-in flip with no number, and Tough It Out never appears anywhere.
audit.why: Undertow is a flat 9s and its cooldown RESETS if Olaf picks the axe up, which is what makes 'stand on the pickup spot' worth doing and turns a 9-second window into a real one. Ragnarok is 100/90/80s. Reckless Swing reaches only 325, the tightest spacing number in the matchup. Tough It Out is a 16s shield plus attack speed, and it is the reason a poke that should have won the trade does not.
audit.corrected: 9s and the pickup reset added to breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t; Ragnarok's 100s added to spikes[2].text and wants.you[2]; Reckless Swing's 325 added to wants.you[0] and breakdown.cooldowns; Tough It Out added to spikes[3].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: MOST VALUABLE FINDING: three fields say Ragnarok makes Olaf CC-immune and conclude that Cassiopeia should simply disengage. Ragnarok grants immunity to DISABLES, not to slows. Miasma's slow and the back-turned half of Petrifying Gaze both still land on an ulting Olaf, which means the correct play is to keep kiting him rather than to abandon the fight.
audit.why: Riot's Ragnarok text: he can activate this ability to become immune to disables for as long as he keeps attacking. Compare Master Yi's Highlander in the same dataset, which says explicitly 'making him immune to all slowing effects' - Riot distinguishes the two, and Ragnarok does not carry the slow clause. The 'keeps attacking' condition matters too: it is not a fire-and-forget duration. So the stun genuinely whiffs, but the kite does not, and the existing text throws away Cassiopeia's actual answer.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text, whys[4], mid and wants.you[2] now say the stun whiffs while the slows still land, and keep the kite as the plan.

audit.whatIsWrong: CHAMP_FULL tldr reads 'Miasma is the anti-dash button - ground his engage and the dive kit becomes a farm bot', and dontsFull[1].d warns about leaving 'the dash window wide open'. Olaf has no dash. This directly contradicts the content layer's own mid text, which correctly says the grounding does almost nothing to him.
audit.why: Riot's kit: Undertow is a thrown axe, Tough It Out is a self-buff, Reckless Swing is a melee hit and Ragnarok is a self-buff. No dash, blink or leap anywhere. content.mid already got this right and deserves credit; the FULL layer was still emitting the generic Cassiopeia grounding line.
audit.corrected: tldr and dontsFull[1].d rewritten around the slow, matching what content.mid already says.

audit.whatIsWrong: The kit file tags Undertow (Q) with a 'grounding' flag.
audit.why: Riot's description says Undertow reduces Armor and Move Speed - a slow and an armour shred, with no grounding. Another tooltip-parser misfire, the third in my slice. It happens not to change Cassiopeia's play since she has no dash to lose, but the armour shred is a real detail the text never mentions.
audit.corrected: No claim that Olaf grounds Cassiopeia appears in my text.

notes: The highest-value correction here is the Ragnarok distinction. Three fields told the player to disengage because Olaf becomes CC-immune; Ragnarok grants immunity to disables, not to slows, so Miasma and the back-turned half of Petrifying Gaze both still land and kiting remains the answer. Riot draws that distinction explicitly in the same dataset — Master Yi's Highlander says 'immune to all slowing effects' while Ragnarok says only 'immune to disables'. Credit where due: content.mid already correctly states that Miasma's grounding does nothing to a dashless Olaf, while the FULL tldr still called Miasma 'the anti-dash button' — the two layers contradicted each other and the content layer was right. Left unverified and unclaimed: whether Ragnarok's disable immunity also cleanses an already-applied Petrifying Gaze stun, and whether Tough It Out's shield fully absorbs a Twin Fang or only reduces it.
